# Contributing

<!-- Generated by seed-golden-context | Last updated: 2026-05-11 -->

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Java | 17 | `sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17` in all module `build.gradle` files |
| Android SDK | compileSdk 35 | Required to build the `android` module; set `ANDROID_HOME` |
| Gradle | Wrapper included | Use `./gradlew` — do not install Gradle separately |

No `.nvmrc` or Node.js required — this is a pure Java/Android project.

## Getting Started

```bash
# Clone
git clone git@github.com:contentful/rich-text-renderer-java.git
cd rich-text-renderer-java

# Build all modules
./gradlew build

# Run all tests
./gradlew test

# Build a specific module
./gradlew :core:build
./gradlew :html:build
./gradlew :android:build
```

## Development Workflow

This is a multi-module Gradle project. The root `build.gradle` applies settings to all subprojects. Each module (`core`, `html`, `android`, `android_sample`) has its own `build.gradle`.

```bash
# Run tests for a single module
./gradlew :core:test
./gradlew :html:test
./gradlew :android:test

# Clean build outputs
./gradlew clean

# Run a specific test class
./gradlew :html:test --tests "HeadingTest"
```

## Testing

- **Framework:** JUnit 4 (`junit:junit:4.13.2`) with Google Truth assertions
- **Android tests:** Robolectric (`org.robolectric:robolectric:4.14.1`) for JVM-based Android unit tests
- **Location:** `<module>/src/test/java/` mirroring the main source structure
- **Run all:** `./gradlew test`
- **Run single module:** `./gradlew :html:test`
- **Run single class:** `./gradlew :html:test --tests "HeadingTest"`

The `html` module includes E2E tests under `html/src/test/java/e2e/` that exercise the full rendering pipeline against fixture data.

Embedded entry and hyperlink rendering cannot be tested with generic fixtures — consumer-side tests are needed for those.

## Commit Convention

This repo uses [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

```
type(scope): description [DX-XXX]
```

Valid types: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `perf`, `ci`, `build`, `revert`

Scope is typically the module name: `core`, `html`, `android`.

Examples:
```
feat(android): add table renderer
fix(html): trim URI whitespace [DX-892]
chore: update codeowners to DX team
```

## Branch Strategy

- `master` — production-stable; all releases are tagged from here
- Feature/fix branches — `feat/...`, `fix/...`, `chore/...`, `release/X.Y.Z`
- Release branches follow the pattern `release/X.Y.Z` and are merged back to `master` via PR

## Release Process

Releases are distributed via [JitPack](https://jitpack.io/#contentful/rich-text-renderer-java). A release is triggered by:

1. Creating a `release/X.Y.Z` branch
2. Bumping versions in root `build.gradle` (project `version`) and individual module `build.gradle` files (`artifactId` version field)
3. Merging to `master` via PR
4. JitPack picks up the new tag/commit automatically

No manual publish step is required — JitPack builds on demand when consumers add the dependency.

## Pull Requests

- Target `master`
- PR title should follow Conventional Commits format (include Jira ticket `[DX-XXX]` where applicable)
- All tests must pass
- CodeQL workflow runs on PRs touching `.github/workflows/`
- Code owners: `@contentful/team-developer-experience` (see `.github/CODEOWNERS`)

## CI/CD

| Job | Trigger | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| CodeQL (Actions) | Push/PR to `master` touching `.github/workflows/**` | Static analysis of GitHub Actions workflow files for security issues |

Note: there is no automated test CI workflow at time of writing — tests are run locally. This is a flagged gap (see PR body).
